request.spec:
Show on each person their cut total: their cuts across every pool they are a member of, added
up (a pool that shows no cuts adds nothing). Show the sheet's cut total: everyone's added up.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their cut total: their cuts across every pool they are a member of, added
up (a pool that shows no cuts adds nothing). Show the sheet's cut total: everyone's added up.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person now shows their cut total, and the sheet shows its cut total. All 4 acceptance tests pass.

**What was added** (only in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`):
- **Per person (`person-cut-total`):** the person's cuts from every pool they belong to, added up. A pool that shows no cuts (because it has no pot or isn't balanced) adds nothing, so the total is `0.00` when there are none.
- **Per sheet (`rollup-cut-total`):** every person's cut total added up. It counts everyone on the sheet, including retired people when "show retired" is off; their cuts are 0.00 anyway.

**Why no server or database change:** the server already works out each pool member's cut, including how rounding leftovers are shared out. The new totals just add up the cuts the pools panel already shows (e.g. Ada gets 0.51 + 0.34 = 0.85), so they always match. They are recomputed whenever the pools are re-read.

**Port:** `bin/e2e` refused to start because something else was already using port 3000. I didn't start that process, so I left it running and ran the test with `PORT=3417 bin/e2e` instead.
